/-!
# Conjecture 10.78

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist a non-Chernikov group which is a product of two Chernikov subgroups?

A *Chernikov group* is a finite extension of a direct product of finitely many Prüfer
(quasicyclic) $p$-groups. Equivalently, it is a group with an abelian subgroup of finite
index that satisfies the minimal condition on subgroups. Here "product" means the setwise
product $AB = G$ of two subgroups $A$ and $B$; neither factor is assumed to be normal.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

  (∃ N : Subgroup G, N.FiniteIndex ∧ IsMulCommutative N) ∧ WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is a *Chernikov group* if it is a finite extension of a direct product of finitely
many Prüfer (quasicyclic) $p$-groups. By Kurosh's theorem on abelian groups with the minimal
condition (see D. J. S. Robinson, *A Course in the Theory of Groups*, Sections 4.2 and 5.4),
this holds if and only if $G$ has an abelian subgroup of finite index and satisfies the minimal
condition on subgroups, that is, there is no infinite strictly descending chain of subgroups
of $G$. We use this characterisation as the definition. In particular every finite group is
Chernikov.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent (Mathlib.GroupTheory.Nilpotent) is the closest existing 'virtually P' predicate but has the wrong P and lacks the Min condition; WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G) and Subgroup.FiniteIndex / IsMulCommutative are the existing primitives the definition is built from. Mathlib's only Prüfer-related content (Dynamics/FixedPoints/Prufer.lean) is a lemma, not a definition of the Prüfer group.
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.78».IsChernikov
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has a notion of Chernikov group, Prüfer/quasicyclic group, or the minimal condition on subgroups as a named predicate (rg for chernikov/cernikov/prüfer/prufer/quasicyclic/virtually returns nothing relevant). The problem is about Chernikov groups, so a predicate is unavoidable.

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isChernikov_multiplicative_int : ¬ IsChernikov (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  rintro ⟨-, h⟩
  refine not_strictAnti_of_wellFoundedLT
    (fun n => AddSubgroup.toSubgroup (AddSubgroup.zmultiples ((2 : ℤ) ^ n))) ?_
  refine strictAnti_nat_of_succ_lt fun n => ?_
  rw [OrderIso.lt_iff_lt, SetLike.lt_iff_le_and_exists]
  refine ⟨AddSubgroup.zmultiples_le_of_mem ?_, 2 ^ n, AddSubgroup.mem_zmultiples _, ?_⟩
  · rw [Int.mem_zmultiples_iff, pow_succ]
    exact dvd_mul_right _ _
  · rw [Int.mem_zmultiples_iff, pow_succ]
    intro h
    have := Int.le_of_dvd (by positivity) h
    nlinarith [pow_pos (show (0 : ℤ) < 2 by norm_num) n]

Does there exist a non-Chernikov group which is a product of two Chernikov subgroups?

That is, is there a group $G$ with subgroups $A$ and $B$ such that $A$ and $B$ are Chernikov
groups, $G = AB = \{ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$, and $G$ is not a Chernikov group? Neither $A$

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no existence question (answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ G [Group G], ∃ A B : Subgroup G, Chernikov A ∧ Chernikov B ∧ (A : Set G) * B = Set.univ ∧ ¬ Chernikov G); 'product' means the setwise product AB = G with neither factor assumed normal (the normal case is Chernikov's classical positive theorem), and Mathlib has no Chernikov-group predicate, so it must be defined in-file (finite extension of a direct product of finitely many Prüfer p-groups, equivalently a virtually abelian group satisfying the minimal condition on subgroups).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the identical, faithful shape `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (A B : Subgroup G), IsChernikov A ∧ IsChernikov B ∧ (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ ∧ ¬ IsChernikov G` with the setwise (non-normal) product, and all encode 'Chernikov' by the standard equivalent characterisation 'abelian subgroup of finite index ∧ minimal condition on subgroups' (c07 uses the equivalent 'normal finite-index abelian subgroup with Min', c03 spells out Min explicitly; all equivalent by Kurosh's theorem plus the normal-core argument). I verified in Lean that the pointwise product membership is `∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, a * b = g` and that `WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)` is literally `WellFounded (· < ·)`, i.e. the minimal condition. c02 was chosen as the base because it has the most complete docstrings and is the only candidate with a non-trivial API test (`Multiplicative ℤ` is not Chernikov), which pins down that the definition encodes Min rather than Max; finite groups being Chernikov is also tested. I lightly edited the docstrings (attributing the equivalence to Kurosh's theorem rather than 'a theorem of Chernikov', and removing the module-docstring claim about the normal case, whose attribution is shaky).

/-!
# Conjecture 10.78

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist a non-Chernikov group which is a product of two Chernikov subgroups?

A *Chernikov group* is a finite extension of a direct product of finitely many Prüfer
(quasicyclic) $p$-groups. Equivalently, it is a group with an abelian subgroup of finite
index that satisfies the minimal condition on subgroups. Here "product" means the setwise
product $AB = G$ of two subgroups $A$ and $B$; neither factor is assumed to be normal.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«10.78»

/--
A group $G$ is a *Chernikov group* if it is a finite extension of a direct product of finitely
many Prüfer (quasicyclic) $p$-groups. By Kurosh's theorem on abelian groups with the minimal
condition (see D. J. S. Robinson, *A Course in the Theory of Groups*, Sections 4.2 and 5.4),
this holds if and only if $G$ has an abelian subgroup of finite index and satisfies the minimal
condition on subgroups, that is, there is no infinite strictly descending chain of subgroups
of $G$. We use this characterisation as the definition. In particular every finite group is
Chernikov.
-/
def IsChernikov (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  (∃ N : Subgroup G, N.FiniteIndex ∧ IsMulCommutative N) ∧ WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)

/-- Every finite group is a Chernikov group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isChernikov_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsChernikov G :=
  ⟨⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance⟩, inferInstance⟩

/-- The infinite cyclic group is not a Chernikov group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isChernikov_multiplicative_int : ¬ IsChernikov (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  rintro ⟨-, h⟩
  refine not_strictAnti_of_wellFoundedLT
    (fun n => AddSubgroup.toSubgroup (AddSubgroup.zmultiples ((2 : ℤ) ^ n))) ?_
  refine strictAnti_nat_of_succ_lt fun n => ?_
  rw [OrderIso.lt_iff_lt, SetLike.lt_iff_le_and_exists]
  refine ⟨AddSubgroup.zmultiples_le_of_mem ?_, 2 ^ n, AddSubgroup.mem_zmultiples _, ?_⟩
  · rw [Int.mem_zmultiples_iff, pow_succ]
    exact dvd_mul_right _ _
  · rw [Int.mem_zmultiples_iff, pow_succ]
    intro h
    have := Int.le_of_dvd (by positivity) h
    nlinarith [pow_pos (show (0 : ℤ) < 2 by norm_num) n]

/--
Does there exist a non-Chernikov group which is a product of two Chernikov subgroups?

That is, is there a group $G$ with subgroups $A$ and $B$ such that $A$ and $B$ are Chernikov
groups, $G = AB = \{ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$, and $G$ is not a Chernikov group? Neither $A$
nor $B$ is assumed to be normal in $G$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.78» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (A B : Subgroup G),
      IsChernikov A ∧ IsChernikov B ∧ (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ ∧
        ¬ IsChernikov G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.78»

items: IsChernikov G is defined as (∃ N : Subgroup G, N.FiniteIndex ∧ IsMulCommutative N) ∧ WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G), i.e. 'virtually abelian and satisfies the minimal condition on subgroups'. This is equivalent to the textbook definition 'finite extension of a direct product of finitely many Prüfer p-groups' by Kurosh's classification of abelian groups with Min together with Chernikov's theorem (Robinson, A Course in the Theory of Groups, §4.2 and §5.4); the direct Prüfer-product formulation was avoided because Mathlib has no Prüfer-group type and it would require a much heavier ∃-over-types-and-MulEquiv encoding. A reviewer should confirm they accept this equivalent characterisation as the definition.
The minimal condition on subgroups is encoded as WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G) (no infinite strictly descending chain of subgroups / every nonempty family of subgroups has a minimal member).

'Product of two subgroups' is the setwise product (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ (open scoped Pointwise), with neither A nor B assumed normal, following the decomposition notes. Since A, B are subgroups this is symmetric (AB = G ⇔ BA = G).
IsChernikov A for A : Subgroup G is evaluated on the coerced subtype ↥A with its induced group structure, i.e. A is Chernikov as a group in its own right.
The existential ranges over G : Type (universe 0), matching the other Kourovka files (1.74, 19.25); Chernikov groups and their products are countable, so this loses nothing.
Two proved @[category test] lemmas are included as API sanity checks for the bespoke definition: every finite group is Chernikov, and Multiplicative ℤ is not Chernikov.

reviewer_notes: Single-slot yes/no existence question; no candidate omitted anything and there were no decomposition objections. Modeling points a reviewer should be aware of: (1) Mathlib has no Chernikov predicate, so `IsChernikov` is defined in-file as 'virtually abelian ∧ WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)'; this is equivalent to 'finite extension of a direct product of finitely many Prüfer p-groups' (Kurosh's theorem on abelian groups with Min; Min is extension-closed; the normal core / divisible part gives the normal finite-index Prüfer-product subgroup). Finite groups count as Chernikov, as in the standard definition — excluding them would trivialise the problem. (2) 'Product' is the setwise product AB = G with neither factor normal, matching the decomposition notes and the intent of the problem. (3) The witness group is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files; this is harmless because Chernikov groups are countable, so any group that is a product of two Chernikov subgroups is countable and has a copy in `Type`. (4) `IsChernikov A` for `A : Subgroup G` is evaluated on the coerced subtype with its induced group structure. Status kept as `research open` per the provided statement metadata.
